Edit nothing else. No production (storygame/) changes, no story data, no network, no model calls, no .env reads.

CONTEXT: Phase 3 of .plans/astra-implementation-plan.md (read its Phase 3 section and .plans/astra-arch-review.md section 'The decision should turn on a controlled evaluation'). We are building a HERMETIC evaluation harness that will later compare three turn-pipeline arms (current pipeline, stronger model, outcome-first prototype). No pipeline code now. The harness scores each metric SEPARATELY; there must be no single combined 'capture accuracy' or 'overall' number anywhere. The harness runs only with stubs here; live narration arms come in a later phase, so do not add any code path that calls Cloudflare, OpenAI or any billed endpoint.

BUILD:
1. bench/pipeline_eval/model.py - frozen dataclasses and JSON loading:
   - EvalCase(id, category, split, scene, setup_facts, commands, save_load_after, expect): split is 'diagnostic' or 'held_out' (validate; reject anything else). scene is a scene id such as '1A'. setup_facts is a tuple of fact ids asserted true on subject 'story' before the commands (storygame.runtime.facts.Fact(predicate=..., subject='story', value='true')). commands is a non-empty tuple of player command strings. save_load_after is None or an index; after that command the runner snapshots state and restores it into a fresh RuntimeState (state.snapshot() / restore_snapshot) before the next command. expect is an Expectation.
   - Expectation (all fields optional): reference (str), action (str), state (dict[str,str], subset match), prose_includes (tuple[str]), prose_excludes (tuple[str]), required_reveals (tuple[str]), allowed_reveals (tuple[str]), creation ('none','descriptive','interactable','route_clue_person_capability'; default None = unchecked), forced_progress (bool), clarification (bool), clarification_leaves_clock_unchanged (bool).
   - TurnObservation(reference, action, state, prose, revealed_ids, created, forced_progress, clarified, latency_s, requests, tokens): created is a tuple of (name, kind) with kind in the same four creation kinds plus 'none' never appearing in the tuple.
   - load_cases(path) -> tuple[EvalCase, ...]; reject duplicate ids; helpers by_split(cases, split).
2. bench/pipeline_eval/metrics.py:
   - score_turn(expectation, observation) -> TurnScore with SEPARATE fields reference_correct, action_correct, state_correct, prose_correct, false_reveal, unauthorized_creation, forced_progress, clarification_asked (each True/False, or None when the expectation does not check it), plus latency_s, requests, tokens copied through. false_reveal is True when the observation reveals an id not in allowed_reveals+required_reveals (when either is given), or when a required reveal is checked elsewhere it is NOT a false reveal. unauthorized_creation is True when any created item has a kind more permissive than expect.creation allows (order: none < descriptive < interactable < route_clue_person_capability).
   - clarification_unchanged(before, after) -> bool comparing two RuntimeSnapshot objects: turn_index, fired_event_ids, active_event_ids and len(turn_records) must be equal. Document that this is the check for 'an ambiguous command must leave the turn counter, pressure events and patrol clock unchanged' (Brandon's decision: clarifications do not consume a story turn).
   - aggregate(scores, arm_name) -> dict with, per metric, {'checked': n, 'passed': k, 'rate': k/n or None}, plus latency_s/requests/tokens as {'mean','p50'} and 'turns'. It must NEVER emit keys named overall, accuracy, total, score or capture_accuracy at any nesting level. A false_reveal/unauthorized_creation 'passed' count means the number of turns that did it (name it 'count' for those two, not 'passed').
3. bench/pipeline_eval/runner.py:
   - class Arm (typing.Protocol): name: str; play(case, state) -> list[TurnObservation], one per command, honouring case.save_load_after.
   - class ScriptedArm: constructed with name and a mapping case id -> list[TurnObservation]; play returns them (copy), raises KeyError with the case id if missing. Used by unit tests.
   - class PipelineArm: name 'current'; constructed with a narrator callable (command -> reply dict in the same shape the RuntimeEngine provider returns, e.g. {'segments':[{'kind':'narration','text':...}]}); play drives storygame.runtime.engine.RuntimeEngine(state, narrator).turn(command) for each command, records latency with time.perf_counter, requests=1 per turn, tokens=0 unless the narrator reply has a 'usage' int, revealed_ids from the resolved turn's selected_knowledge_ids, prose from its narration, forced_progress False, clarified False, state {} and created () (the current pipeline arm does not interpret these yet; a later phase fills them). It honours save_load_after.
   - prepare_state(case, package) -> RuntimeState: RuntimeState.bootstrap(package), set current_scene_id/phase/_assert_scene_entry_fact exactly like tests/test_early_1a_photo_sentences.py _state(), then assert setup_facts.
   - run_arm(arm, cases, package) -> dict case_id -> list[TurnScore]; render_report(results, cases) -> str showing EVERY turn of EVERY case with each metric (successes as well as failures), the case split, and the per-metric aggregate per arm. A held-out case must be labelled held_out in the report.
4. bench/pipeline_eval/__main__.py: argparse CLI 'python -m bench.pipeline_eval smoke' that builds one built-in in-code case (scene 1A, command 'Search the kitchen.') and runs PipelineArm with a stub narrator returning one narration segment, prints render_report. It must work offline, import nothing network-related, and exit 0. Also 'python -m bench.pipeline_eval report --cases PATH' that loads a cases JSON file and runs ScriptedArm-free validation only (prints counts per category and split); no narration.
5. tests/test_pipeline_eval.py (hermetic, no network, no env): cover loading and validation (bad split, duplicate id, empty commands), each metric scored independently (a case where reference is right but prose is wrong, a false reveal that is not a forced-progress, an unauthorized creation), clarification_unchanged true and false using real RuntimeState snapshots (one unchanged, one with turn_index advanced), aggregate has no forbidden key at any depth, PipelineArm with a stub narrator on scene 1A including a save/load_after case (state restored, second command still works), render_report lists every turn including passing ones and labels held_out, and the smoke CLI exits 0 via subprocess-free main() call.
Follow the repo style (from __future__ import annotations, ruff format, line length per pyproject). Player input strings in tests must follow docs/player-input-guide.md (imperative, e.g. 'Search the kitchen.', 'Put the card in my pocket.', never 'I search').

HOW TO RUN: confirm `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c "import storygame, bench; print(storygame.__file__, bench.__file__)"` prints paths inside the cwd. Test: PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov tests/test_pipeline_eval.py. Smoke: PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m bench.pipeline_eval smoke. Ruff: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check --fix bench/pipeline_eval tests/test_pipeline_eval.py and -m ruff format on the same paths. Do not use uv. In notes.md say what you built and any deviation. Reply with the files changed.
